correctness.rationale: For b>=3 odd and q odd, if sigma(N)/N=(sigma(q^b)+1)/q^b with q^b|N, an even host is excluded by the 3/2 (q>=5) or 2 (q=3 with 6|N) abundancy bound. Then sigma(N) is odd, since sigma(q^b) is even; an odd host with odd divisor sum has only even prime exponents, so N is a square. If N=q^(b+1)p^(2a), let S=sigma(q^b), H=sigma(q^(b+1))=S+q^(b+1). Divisibility monotonicity gives p>=S. The exact ratio implies H*sigma(p^(2a-1))=(q-1)p^(2a). As p>=S>q and sigma(p^(2a-1))==1 mod p, p^(2a)|H. But S^2>H, a contradiction. The next possible square-host shared exponent is >=b+3. Independently checked rational identities and size inequalities on many q,b, but this is a symbolic all-prime proof.
